subject: Microburst granularity, staggered minimums, and reconciliation tickets for committed credits
messages:
From: Alan Cho <alan.cho@cloudretail.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cloudretail.com
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on microburst credits & minimums (CloudRetail)

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the call earlier — Alan here from CloudRetail. Before we finalize the commitment, procurement has two technical billing asks we need clarified for the SOW:

1) We do a lot of short interleaved streaming calls (100-500ms each) across many users. How do you quantify "microburst credits" vs the monthly minimum? If we commit to 200k tokens/month reserved, will a thousand tiny calls each billed at a floor blow past that quickly?

2) What rounding rule applies when a single streaming connection interleaves multiple logical sessions (prefixes) — do you aggregate per-connection or per-session?

Procurement also wants a simple reconciliation flow if consumption appears inflated (we'll open a ticket with usage IDs). Could you send a short example invoice snippet and a reconciliation SLA?

Thanks — Alan
Alan Cho
Head of Platform Engineering, CloudRetail
alan.cho@cloudretail.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Cho <alan.cho@cloudretail.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on microburst credits & minimums (CloudRetail)

Alan — thanks, good questions. High-level answers below and I attached a CSV with a couple of worked examples.

1) Microburst credits vs monthly minimums:
- Reserved commitments buy you a pool of tokens (200k tokens/month in your case). We meter actual usage and deduct from the pool. Microbursts are not a separate "bucket" unless you add the optional microburst protection add-on; without it, each microburst consumes tokens from the same pool.
- To avoid unexpected consumption from many sub-second calls we recommend enabling prefix aggregation (see #2) and an interleaving window of 30s for short lived streams. That will aggregate small requests that share a prefix and bill them as a single conversation window where appropriate.

2) Aggregation and rounding:
- Default rule: billing happens per logical session (conversation/prefix). For streaming endpoints we use a 10-second ephemeral heartbeat window (configurable per-customer). If two frames from the same logical session are within 10s, they are aggregated into the same billing event.
- Rounding: tokens are billed in 0.25-token increments for streaming frames to balance precision and invoice readability. For non-streaming (batch) calls we bill per-whole-token.

Reconciliation & tickets:
- If CloudRetail suspects overcharge, open a support reconciliation ticket with: sample request IDs, timestamps, and the affected route/model. We have a 5-business-day SLA to triage and a 10-business-day SLA for a final reconciliation (credit or explanation).
- I've attached the CSV that shows how three microburst patterns map to billed tokens under the default 10s aggregation + 0.25-token rounding.

I'll loop in Jonas for the edge-case where your front-end multiplexes many logical users over a single TCP connection — the aggregation heuristic can be tuned to prefer "per-user" semantics if you pass an identity token in the request metadata.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Attachments: microburst-credit-examples.csv (CSV, 12KB); proposed-rounding-policy.md (text, 3KB)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Cho <alan.cho@cloudretail.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 12:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on microburst credits & minimums (CloudRetail)

Alan — quick technical follow-up from infra. Two practical knobs we expose that will matter:

1) Aggregation key precedence: by default we use (customer_id > prefix > connection_id). If you are multiplexing user sessions on a single connection, pass the per-user id in the request header X-CR-User to guarantee per-user aggregation.

2) Staggered minimums: you said you wanted a blended pricing for streaming vs batch. We can model a "staggered minimum" where 60% of the committed pool is reserved for streaming-priced tokens (0.25 rounding) and 40% for batch-priced tokens (whole token). That reduces cross-use bleed and helps predictability.

3) Fair-use reconciliation: as Grace said, open a ticket; our billing exports include per-request delta logs (request_id, model, prompt_tokens, gen_tokens, aggregation_key). If a microburst pattern looks artificially inflating consumption (e.g., tiny frames creating extra model context due to repeated prefix), we can apply a one-time corrective credit up to 5% of monthly commitment while the root cause is fixed.

If you want, we can send a short addendum to the SOW that codifies the aggregation window (default 10s), the rounding increments (0.25 streaming / 1.0 batch), and the staged credit policy for first-month anomalies.

Jonas Weber
Director, Serving Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
